hypotheses.justification: The theorem is still true when J is empty. Mathlib defines `F.sections` as `{u : ∀ j, F.obj j | ∀ {j j'} (f : j ⟶ j'), F.map f (u j) = u j'}`. If `J` is empty, then `Jᵒᵖ` is empty, so the unique dependent function `fun j => isEmptyElim j.unop` is a section: the compatibility condition holds vacuously. So `F.sections.Nonempty` holds with no further hypotheses. The current proof uses `[Nonempty J]` in only one place: the library lemma `IsCofinal.exists_monotone_nat` (CofinalSequence.lean) needs it to get a nonempty cofinal set. The fix is to start the proof with `cases isEmpty_or_nonempty J`. In the empty case, close the goal with the empty section above. In the nonempty case, run the existing proof unchanged, since the instance is now available. The other hypotheses are all needed. Without `IsDirectedOrder`, take J = {a, b, c, d} with c, d ≤ a, b and every F.obj equal to Bool. Let a→c, b→c and a→d be the identity and b→d be negation. All maps are bijective, so F is Mittag-Leffler, and J is finite, so it is a countable cofinal subset of itself. But a section would need x_a = x_b and x_a = ¬x_b, so there is none. Pointwise nonemptiness, the Mittag-Leffler condition and countability are the standard necessary assumptions.
